explicitUncertainty.text: **A reconstruction, not the paper's data.** I could not read the paper's parameter tables, so the six curves use rounded illustrative three-compartment models of my own (orders of magnitude only; fentanyl $V_1$ and $V_{ss}$ follow commonly quoted round values), with an infusion that holds the plasma concentration constant. Left: context-sensitive half-time against infusion duration, 1 min to 8 h on a log axis, for the six drugs; the dots mark the duration you choose. Right: bars of the half-time at that duration beside each drug's terminal half-life (log scale): they are not the same, and the ranking changes with the duration. The readout compares the span of the model values with the 1 to 306 minutes reported in the abstract. Switch the infusion to a constant rate to see how the definition matters.

Parameter sets are illustrative, not the paper's; the paper's exact simulation scheme (including whether the infusion held a constant plasma concentration, as the definition is usually stated) was not checked beyond its abstract. Only qualitative features should be compared: the half-time differs from the elimination half-life, grows with duration at different rates for different drugs, and the ranking of drugs can change. Not a guide to drug choice or dosing.

queue.name: Computerized Transverse Axial Scanning (Tomography): Part 1

explicitUncertainty.text: Hounsfield described a scanner in which a narrow X-ray beam and detector traverse a slice of the head, take a row of transmission readings, then rotate by a small step and repeat; a computer reconstructs the absorption in a matrix of small elements from the whole set of readings and displays it as a picture, together with numerical values relative to water. Because the readings are digitised and used quantitatively, the system distinguishes tissues whose X-ray absorption differs by only about a per cent — grey and white matter, blood clot, cerebrospinal fluid — which a radiograph, where the shadow of bone and of the depth superimpose, cannot show. (Parameters of the first scanner — about $80\times80$ picture elements and of the order of $160$ readings at each of $180$ one-degree steps — are as commonly reported and are marked unverified.)
